label: rem:ns-classical-formulation
title: The classical regularity question for the Navier--Stokes equation
html:
Evaluating the q-NS system at q = 1 recovers the classical incompressible Navier--Stokes equation mapped over \mathbb{R}^3:

  \partial_t v + (v \cdot \nabla)v = -\nabla p + \nu\Delta v,
  \qquad \nabla \cdot v = 0,
  \qquad v|_{t=0} = v_0.

Standard analysis asks whether supplying perfectly smooth initial data v_0 \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3) featuring \nabla \cdot v_0 = 0 alongside finite energy guarantees a smooth global solution, or whether a singularity triggers abruptly in finite time.

The defined NS obstruction \mathrm{NS}(A) resolves this exactly using the categorical properties native to the quantum universe. \mathrm{NS}(A) = 0 enforces regularity. \mathrm{NS}(A) \neq 0 guarantees blowup. The obstruction rests on \chi(A).
